newsitem.title: CANADA: Seagram reports a profit after year-ago loss.
newsitem.headline: Seagram reports a profit after year-ago loss.

text.p: Seagram Co. Ltd., the Canadian beverage and entertainment giant, said Wednesday it earned more than $160 million in the latest quarter as its juice, spirits and music businesses reversed a year ago loss.
The company said it earned $161 million, or 43 cents a share, in its fiscal second quarter ended Dec. 31 vs. a loss of $26 million, or 7 cents a share, a year earlier.

The Montreal-based firm said the results included a $64 million pre-tax gain on the sale in December of its Universal's book publishing unit while the previous year's quarter included a $290 million restructuring charge for Seagram's beverage operations. Excluding the charge, Seagram had an operating profit of $185 million or 50 cents a share in the year-ago second quarter.
Seagram said all three of its major businesses performed better in the quarter.
"Seagram made additional progress this quarter towards our goal of sustained growth in all three of our businesses," Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr said.

"Seagram Beverage Group recorded strong North American growth, improved international earnings and higher margins. Spirits and Wine Group earnings improved despite extremely difficult market conditions in Europe and Asia Pacific which have continued into the current quarter."

"Universal's investment in its Music Group's new labels and artists this past year led to significantly higher revenues and profits in the quarter," Bronfman said. "Universal's theme parks also continued to perform well following the opening of two new attractions last spring."

Seagram, which purchased an 80 percent stake of Universal from Japanese Electonics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. in 1995, said earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or cash flow, rose 10 percent in the quarter to $530 million.
Such earnings are a key indicator of financial performance, particularly in the entertainment industry where analysts pay more attention to cash generated by operations than net income.
Seagram said Universal, which includes film, television, music and theme parks, reported a 13 percent increase in cash flow stemming from improved results in music and theme parks.

The company has been investing heavily in new artists and labels over the past year to bolster its music unit, scoring hits with records from artists such as Bush, No Doubt, Snoop Doggy Dogg, and Counting Crows.
The company is also planning a new theme park in Japan and is investing in new luxury hotels in Orlando, Fla.
For the six months ended in December, Seagram earned $327 million, or 88 cents a share, after unusual items vs. $40 million or 11 cents a share a year ago.
Seagram's stock was unchanged at $39.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
